claims.text: Applying a thin hafnium-enriched surface coating to high-entropy boride components will reduce corrosion by molten aluminum.
Hf-containing high-entropy borides can be produced as sintered ceramic components.
A thin hafnium-enriched coating should be deposited on the boride component.
The proposed coating may be deposited by sputtering, chemical vapor deposition, or another coating method.
Hot-dip aluminum-plating operation involves molten aluminum at around 660 °C in dynamic contact with the component.
The coating will form a stable hafnium-rich interfacial layer, potentially comprising HfO2 or Hf-Al compounds.
A hafnium-derived transition layer can chemically bond a hafnium coating to its substrate.
The hafnium-rich interfacial layer will impede direct contact between molten aluminum and the bulk boride.
At the operating temperature, hafnium from the coating will diffuse slightly into the underlying boride matrix.
Coating-substrate interdiffusion can form an alloy transition layer.
The interfacial intermetallic or oxide layer will act as a barrier to aluminum penetration and subsequent corrosion.
The barrier may protect the boride by chemically binding aluminum or by forming a passivating oxide film.
Hafnium-coated components will have lower corrosion depths than uncoated boride components under identical molten-aluminum exposure.
Hafnium-coated components will show reduced weight changes relative to uncoated boride components under identical molten-aluminum exposure.
The protective effect should persist over typical hot-dip aluminum-plating temperatures and exposure durations.
Mechanical wear, insufficient coating thickness, coating nonuniformity, process variability, or impurities may compromise protection.

A controlled comparison will expose coated and uncoated high-entropy borides to molten aluminum at approximately 660 °C and measure corrosion depth, mass change, phase composition, and hafnium depth profiles.
The hypothesis will be falsified if the coated group does not exhibit a statistically significant reduction in both corrosion depth and weight change relative to the uncoated control.
